desktopOnly.title: The booth editor needs a larger screen
desktopOnly.body: The 3D editor is built for a mouse and a wide viewport — dragging furniture, marquee selection, and the property inspector all need room to work. We would rather tell you that than hand you a broken screen.
desktopOnly.requirement: Requires a viewport at least {{width}} px wide. A laptop or desktop works; so does a tablet in landscape.

outstanding.title: Outstanding balance
outstanding.body: Everything still owed across your issued invoices, added up. Paid, cancelled and draft invoices are not counted.
outstanding.note: A part-paid invoice contributes only what is left on it, not its full total.

overdue.title: Overdue
overdue.body: Issued invoices whose due date has passed and which are not yet settled in full.

history.title: Payment history
history.body: Every payment recorded against this invoice, oldest first. A deposit and the later balance appear as separate entries.

escalate.title: Escalating to a chief
escalate.body: Your project manager is your first point of contact and sees everything about your stand. Escalate when you need a decision they cannot make, or when you have not heard back.
escalate.note: Once you escalate, that manager stays in your contact list and you can message them normally.

revisions.title: Revision rounds
revisions.body: Each round of changes you ask for uses one. Asking in words and sending a furniture layout both count as one round.
revisions.note: Approving the design or asking a question in Messages costs nothing.

propose.title: Proposing a layout
propose.body: Arrange the furniture how you would like it and send it to your project manager. They apply it to the design or explain why not.
propose.note: Only furniture is yours to move. Walls, fascia and lighting stay as your designer set them, whatever you drag.

flow.title: How an invoice moves
flow.body: Draft while you edit it, issued once sent to the client, paid when the balance reaches zero. Void takes an issued invoice out of play.
flow.note: Record payment logs a deposit or instalment; Mark paid settles whatever is left in one entry. Both appear in the client's payment history.

review.title: Reviewing a client layout
review.body: Preview swaps the canvas to the client's version so you can look at it. Apply merges their furniture into the current design as a new draft.
review.note: Only furniture crosses over. Any structure you have changed since they started is kept.
